briefNote: Three streams, held separately. The client is described by a deficit, not a topic. Topic-similarity matching returns peers, and peers have already solved their own version of it. A qualifier link replaces the pitch: the tool routes, the quiz sorts.

icps.name: Client · Founder in transition
icps.note: The form that carried them has ended and they know it before anyone else does. Income runs on their own name, or the next thing is being born under their hands. Three or four real things going and no sentence that makes them one thing. They do not look impressive on a profile. They look stuck. That is the signal. Do not pitch. Route to the quiz.
terms: ("between ventures" OR "next chapter" OR "former founder") AND founder
(holonic OR integral OR "conscious entrepreneur" OR polymath OR evolutionary) AND (founder OR "ex-founder")
"fractional" AND (CMO OR COO OR CTO OR CPO)
("conscious tech" OR "conscious deep tech") AND (founder OR building)
(visionary OR "systems architect" OR "system architect") AND founder
("what's next" OR "figuring out") AND ("former founder" OR "ex-founder")
(regenerative OR sovereignty OR "new earth") AND (founder OR entrepreneur)
("stepped back" OR "wound down" OR "shut down") AND founder
(web3 OR decentralized OR DAO) AND ("ex-founder" OR "between")
"solopreneur" AND ("next chapter" OR pivoting OR reinventing)

icps.name: Sweet spot · Practitioners who serve founders
icps.note: Coaches, studio operators, accelerator leads, community builders, agency founders who have done the work on themselves. Peers and partners, never prospects. The screening question decides everything: ask what they uniquely bring. A process answer means not ready. A who-they-are answer means ready. One yes here carries the method to a whole client base. The complementary shape wanted most is the grounded builder-operator, closer to execution and ordinary business physics.
terms: ("founder coach" OR "executive coach") AND (founders OR entrepreneurs)
(conscious OR integral OR holonic) AND (coach OR facilitator)
(mentor OR advisor) AND ("zone of genius" OR uniqueness)

icps.name: Altitude · Studio & program operators
icps.note: Running a venture studio, accelerator, or founder program successfully, and conscious about how they run it. Not a session. The technology, the platform, the frameworks, the investment thesis. Rare, and mostly already known. Flag one when it appears.
terms: ("venture studio" OR "startup studio") AND ("managing partner" OR founder)
("founder collective" OR "founders collective") AND (partner OR founder)
(conscious OR regenerative OR evolutionary) AND "venture studio"

exclusions.label: builds their own typology system
exclusions.pattern: typology|psychometric|personality (test|system|profil|assessment)|human design|enneagram|\bmbti\b|16personalities|astrolog|archetype system|profiling system|assessment tool|categorization system|talent assessment
exclusions.note: Day 167, Yulia Winslow. The closest match on topic and structurally unable to buy: their premise is that self-report is unreliable, which is the premise the whole offer rests on.

templates.not_yet: HOLD. High transition, low mirror fidelity: the pain is real and the offer is not yet perceivable. Tribe v6.1 calls this a not-yet, not a buyer. Do not send. Set a re-touch date or let be.

caps.note: Day 169, Sasha's call. 80/week sits under LinkedIn's observed ~100/week platform ceiling; the weekly binds before the daily (4 days at 20 spends the week). Real risk is acceptance rate, not volume: below acceptRateFloor, cut volume rather than push. Ramp the first week on new copy (rampFirstWeek/day) before running at 20.

mfLexicon.note: Mirror-fidelity signal. Tribe v6.1: MF is the whole product, and a person can only buy what they can already see. These words are a person's own public evidence that the faculty is present. Tier 1 is near-zero false positive. Tier 3 is hypothesis under test — measure yield per term before trusting it.

tiers.label: adjacent, under test
tiers.caution: Sasha's own flag: impact/social entrepreneurs may be too rational or aspirational. Aspiration is not fidelity. Hold as hypothesis until the bench measures yield.

streamMarkers.note: These read high on MF but mark the next octave, not the client. They route to stream 3, never to the client template.

mfLexicon.law: Technology 138 — The Faculty Precedes the Fidelity. The lexicon detects the faculty (the organ), not the fidelity (the reading it produces). A peer has the organ too, which is why the cross is required.
mfLexicon.homonymWarning: Day 171, learned from live X-ray. Rare is not enough; a marker must also be UNAMBIGUOUS. 'holonic' mostly returns employees of companies named Holonic. 'integral' collides with ordinary English ('an integral part of') and with Integral Group. Bare single words with a common-English or company-name twin have far lower real precision than their rarity suggests. Prefer the disambiguated multi-word form.

watchlist.note: Not a score and not a class. These words flag a profile for Sasha's own eyes: open it, watch them speak, decide. A word here is a costly public signal - someone willing to say a socially expensive true thing under their own name - which reads on Consent (Technology 123, axis 7: willingness to be seen and altered), not on faculty. Never auto-templated, never auto-connected.

"plant medicine" AND (facilitator OR guide OR practitioner)
watchlist.howToRun: These are not in the stream dropdown by design: the watch lane is judged by Sasha, not scored. Paste one into the search-term field, run it, then open the profiles the tool sorts to the top.

queryRotation.note: Per-query exhaustion is the real ceiling, not pool size. LinkedIn returns roughly 100 results per query without Sales Navigator, and a repeat run returns the same people. Rotate: run 4-6 terms per sitting, not all of them, and watch the Learnings tab by search term. When a term's new-people count collapses, it is spent; retire it and add a variant.
queryRotation.retireWhen: new-people yield on a re-run drops below ~20% of its first run

Crawl your own connections — unaffected by the limit

brief.sendableText:
One update. The last brief was right about who I want, and missing the thing that costs me most: a kind of person who looks perfect and cannot buy.

**The expensive miss.** Someone whose company just ended, genuinely between chapters, in real pain, actively looking. Everything I asked you for. And they cannot use what I do, because using it means being able to take in an accurate description of yourself and act on it, and that capacity is not there yet. The call is good. Nothing follows. I have lost more time to this person than to any obviously wrong match, because nothing about the intro looks wrong.

So here is how to tell the difference, and it is visible in their own words.

**What tells you the capacity is present.** People describe themselves in the vocabulary of what they have actually developed. When someone writes any of these about themselves, unprompted, treat it as evidence about the person, not as a topic I like:

holonic · integral · evolutionary · polymath · zone of genius · sovereignty

Slightly noisier, still strong: conscious · conscious tech · conscious deep tech · visionary · system architect · mystic · sacred geometry · new earth

Weaker and unproven, send them but tell me you are testing: decentralization · web3 · modular · social or impact entrepreneurship. My honest read is that some of these people are still more aspirational than developed, and I would rather find out than assume.

**Now the important part: never send me those words on their own.** Someone with the vocabulary and no transition is my peer, and peers are exactly what the first six intros were. The words are one of three things and I need all three in the same person:

1. the vocabulary, which says the capacity is there
2. income that already runs on their own name
3. a form that is actually ending

Any one of the three missing and it is not my client. All three present and it is worth an introduction even if their profile looks unimpressive, which it usually will.

**Words that mark a different conversation.** Venture studio, founder collective, accelerator, startup studio. These people have the capacity and are running their own vehicle. That is not a session, it is infrastructure and thesis. Send them, and tell me that is what they are.

**One flag, and I do not want you to judge it.** If someone works publicly in cannabis or plant medicine, show me regardless of everything above. Saying that under your own name on LinkedIn costs something, and I want to see who is willing to pay it. I will decide what it means.

**Do not try to read their inner state.** Surface people on what is observable: the words they use about themselves, whether income runs on their own name, whether the form they were in is ending. I do the readiness screen myself after the intro. Guessing at "ripe" or "not ripe" from a profile is my job, not yours, and the three signals above are the whole of what I need you to see.

**On volume: send more, not fewer.** The three signals are a sorting rule, not a scarcity rule. There are far more of these people than either of us has been finding, and the first six intros were too few to learn from. I would rather score twenty and be wrong about twelve than receive three perfect ones a month.

**Studio and program operators are actively wanted.** Last brief called them rare and said flag one when you see it. Sharper now: I want them. Not as a session, as infrastructure and thesis. If someone runs a venture studio, an accelerator or a founder program and runs it consciously, that is a conversation I am ready for, and I have spent twenty years inside collectives of exactly that shape.

**Still true from last time:** exclude anyone building their own typology, personality or human-categorization system. Use findyourtoptalent.com/quiz rather than my offer when you describe me. Practitioners who serve founders are peers and partners, never prospects, and the question that sorts them is what they uniquely bring, not what their method is.
